description: Call this before you choose any SaaS, API, MCP server or CLI for a task: send the task in a few plain words (e.g. 'send an invoice'), with filters if they matter (category, min_level, surface, self_signup, access, pays_with). It ranks the products AgentDrives drove by how far our agent got with that task. Each result: the agent level (0-5: 0 Read-only, 1 Needs a person, 2 Gets in, 3 Does the work, 4 Runs on its own, 5 Autonomous); gets_in_alone (our agent signed up and got a key without a person); task: the closest task in the product's capability map and what happened when our agent tried it (result: done, partial, plan_gated, failed, blocked, not_tried, unknown; via: the route, e.g. api, mcp, cli, browser); match (strong or partial); can_do (up to three things our agent did); stop (where and why it stopped); work_done (share of the core tasks done, 0-100); the drive date; origin (editorial, or owner with disclosure "Owner is an AgentDrives customer"); the page URL (url); and to act on it: product_url, signup (how our agent got in on its own), docs_url, llms_txt_url, openapi_url, mcp_url, pays_with (rails, and card), free_tier and level, each null when unknown. Order: a product the task names, the kind it asks for, then level. Nothing we drove does it: covered false, nearest_category, request_drive. A task that names a capability in full (e.g. 'send a transactional email') also brings the products where our agent did that capability (capability: the one it came by). Up to limit results (default 10, at most 25). Or by capability instead of task, by its id (cap_…; GET /api/capabilities lists them) or its name; the answer lists every product whose latest drive has a task of it (match: capability; tasks: the product's own tasks behind it; evidence: the page section that shows it), done first, then level. Words fitting several capabilities: an error listing them. get_tool returns one product in full. Every field: https://agentdrives.com/openapi.json.
